issue_context.title: Strange behavior with route reusage
issue_context.body:
<!--

-->

## 🐛 Bug Report

By reusing the same route inside more than one plugins, I've noticed that the second time the route is registered, its URL is somehow prefixed by the previous plugin. I'm not sure if this behavior is intentional or a bug.

## To Reproduce

```js
const fastify = require('fastify')({ logger: true })

const route = {
  method: 'GET',
  url: '/',
  async handler(request, reply) {
    return { hello: 'world' }
  },
}

async function v1Plugin(fastify) {
  fastify.route(route)
}

async function v2Plugin(fastify) {
  fastify.route(route)
}

fastify.register(v1Plugin, { prefix: '/api/v1' })
fastify.register(v2Plugin, { prefix: '/api/v2' })

const start = async () => {
  try {
    await fastify.listen(3000)
    console.log(fastify.printRoutes())
    fastify.log.info(`server listening on ${fastify.server.address().port}`)
  } catch (err) {
    fastify.log.error(err)
    process.exit(1)
  }
}

start()
```

## Expected behavior

I was expecting this output:
```
└── /
    └── api/v
        ├── 1 (GET)
        │   └── / (GET)
        └── 2 (GET)
            └── / (GET)
```

I got this instead:
```
└── /
    └── api/v
        ├── 1 (GET)
        │   └── / (GET)
        └── 2/api/v1/ (GET)
```

And I can "fix" that by cloning the `route` object and redefining the `url` property:
```js
fastify.route({ ...route, url: '/' })
```

## Your Environment

- *node version*: 12
- *fastify version*: ^3.4.1
- *os*: Linux

review_comments: This is a shallow clone. Shouldn't `rfdc` be used here?
I thought that a shallow one should be enough, but maybe we need a deep clone because of this https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/7369e7e3f0e881afecb5cf8854afb03edc708b83/lib/route.js#L185

In fact, isn't those line the issue: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/lib/route.js#L176-L179 ?
We are mutating the option object.

Right. The issue is that properties of the passed in options object get mutated, thereby mutating the original passed by reference object. To solve the issue, each route should have its own copy of the passed in object.
Yes, but cloning the initial opts, we are fixing this issue. It is ok now to assign to opts since it is locally scoped to that closure. I am still not sure that a deep clone is needed, though.

I don't know enough. If you say this is the solution, then it is the solution.

👍

Based on those lines, we are mutating/assigning only first level props. I think for this specific mutation it is fine to have a shallow copy using the spread operator. But of course, I could be wrong :)
In this case shallow copy is OK because regarding the functions and object you're already re-using the route object, so you assume that those are references and not copy. It's ok to me.
@fox1t Can you please add a comment with the explanation you did in: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2569#discussion_r492007037?
